svg.text: A modern editorial overview of the Land of the Rising Sun

text.tspan: Japan is an island nation in East Asia, located in the
northwest Pacific Ocean. It stretches over 3,000 km
from north to south across four main islands: Hokkaido,
Honshu, Shikoku, and Kyushu.
With a population of approximately 124 million, Japan
is renowned for its rich cultural heritage, technological
innovation, and distinctive blend of ancient traditions
and modern life. The country is known worldwide for its
cuisine, anime, automotive industry, and high standard
of living.
Tokyo, the capital, is the world's most populous
metropolitan area, blending ultramodern skyscrapers
with historic temples and traditional shops.
Japan's unique position as an archipelago at the convergence of tectonic plates has shaped both its dramatic
volcanic landscape and its resilient culture. From the snow-capped peaks of Mount Fuji to the tropical beaches
of Okinawa, the nation offers extraordinary geographic diversity within a compact area.
Japan is the world's third-largest economy by nominal
GDP. Over the past decade, the economy has faced
headwinds including an aging population, deflationary
pressures, and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.
Key industries include automotive manufacturing,
electronics, robotics, and precision instruments.
Japan remains a global leader in innovation and holds
one of the world's highest standards of living.
The recent decline in nominal GDP partly reflects
yen depreciation and demographic challenges rather
than pure contraction in output.

svg.text: Japan 2015–2024 | Source: World Bank / IMF estimates
Non-Japanese residents account for ≈2.5% of the population — a growing share driven by labour migration.
The foreign-born population has risen from 1.1% in 2010 to over 2.5% in 2024.
Ancient temples, bamboo groves, geisha districts
Street food capital, Dotonbori, Osaka Castle
Peace Memorial, floating torii gate, Itsukushima Shrine
Iconic volcanic peak, hot springs, Lake Ashi
Powder snow, lavender fields, Sapporo, seafood
Sources: World Bank, IMF World Economic Outlook (2024), Statistics Bureau of Japan, Japan National Tourism Organization.
All figures are estimates and rounded for clarity. Nominal GDP figures in current US dollars may vary by source due to exchange-rate fluctuations.
